title: The ALMA-ATOMS survey: A sample of weak hot core candidates identified through line stacking
question: Identify hot cores in the ALMA-ATOMS sample with molecular line stacking, especially weak-emission candidates, to provide one of the largest hot core candidate samples

data.arrays: ACA and 12-m array observed; this work uses 12-m array data
data.sensitivity: mean 1 sigma below 10 mJy/beam per channel (line); 0.4 mJy/beam (continuum)

what.value: Strong sample of 60 hot cores previously identified in ATOMS

evidence.quote: 60 of which are identical to the strong sample previously identified by (cite: 2022MNRAS.511.3463Q)

what.value: LTE-fitted column densities of the 60 strong hot cores, used for comparison with stacking results

evidence.quote: with those derived by (cite: 2022MNRAS.511.3463Q) through LTE fitting for the 60 strong hot cores.
The distances from the Sun are compiled in (cite: 2020MNRAS.496.2790L).

what.value: Typical COM line width of ~5 km/s (FWHM) in strong hot cores, used to set the integration range

evidence.loc: 3.1.5 Integrated intensity maps of stacked cubes
evidence.quote: for the strong sample of hot cores is approximately 5 km s$^{-1}$ (cite: 2020MNRAS.496.2790L)

what.value: Molecular line spectroscopic data (rest frequencies etc.)

evidence.quote: All necessary molecular line information from the Jet Propulsion Laboratory

what.value: Previously identified molecular species in G9.62+0.19, used to label the source-stacked template spectrum

evidence.quote: We fit the template spectrum with the emissions of species already identified from G9.62+0.19

external_data.citation: Liu et al. 2020b (cite: 2020MNRAS.496.2790L); Peng et al. 2022 (cite: 2022MNRAS.512.4419P)

recipe.goal: Build standard hot core spectrum of G9.62+0.19 with XCLASS
recipe.method: Extract peak spectra of G9.62+0.19 cores C1-C3 with CASA, fit with XCLASS assuming LTE, adopt fitted parameters as standard for each species, and model a noise-free standard spectrum
key_parameters: Standard parameters from C1 for CH3OH, CH3OCHO, C2H5OH, CH3OCH3, CH3CHO; text says CH3COCH3 and C2H5OH from C2 and C3 respectively
assumptions: LTE valid because hot core densities exceed the ~1e6 cm-3 critical density
Adopted transitions are optically thin in the standard spectrum and assumed so in other hot cores
In the optically thin limit, beam dilution scales column density and intensity equally so their ratio is unchanged

recipe.goal: Select unblended transitions and derive stacking weights
recipe.method: Keep transitions detected in G9.62+0.19 hot cores and unblended with other molecules; weight each by its peak brightness temperature on the XCLASS noise-free model spectrum
key_parameters: Flux-to-brightness-temperature conversion T = 1.222e3 I/(nu^2 theta_maj theta_min), I in mJy/beam, nu in GHz, beam axes in arcsec
CH3OH 2(1)-2(1) at 97582.898 MHz excluded from stacking

recipe.goal: Cut out and resample line cubes to a common velocity grid
recipe.method: For each source and transition, cut a ~60 km/s cube centred on the rest frequency shifted by V_LSR, convert frequency to velocity, and resample to 1.25 km/s channels
key_parameters: Cube bandwidth ~60 km/s; velocity resolution 1.25 km/s; central frequency nu_c = nu_0 (1 - V_LSR/c)

recipe.goal: Weighted stacking of transitions per species per source
recipe.method: Average the resampled cubes of all transitions of a species with weights W_k: D = sum(W_k D_k)/sum(W_k)
key_parameters: Weights W_k from Table 1 (peak Tb of XCLASS model)
assumptions: Optimal weighting assumes transition intensities proportional to the template and equal noise

recipe.goal: Make moment 0 maps of the stacked cubes
recipe.method: Integrate the stacked cubes over +/-5 km/s
key_parameters: Integration range +/-5 km/s, chosen to match typical COM FWHM of ~5 km/s in strong hot cores

recipe.goal: Identify hot core candidates from moment 0 maps
recipe.method: Visual identification of strong (>~5 sigma), compact CH3OH emission; cores also need at least one other COM
key_parameters: Compact = round morphology with central brightest part unresolved or partly resolved

recipe.goal: Measure core sizes and peak fluxes with 2D Gaussian fits
recipe.method: 2D Gaussian fit of the CH3OH moment 0 map of each of the 100 cores with CASA imfit; same procedure for the other six species
key_parameters: Beam-deconvolved size, position angle, peak and integrated flux adopted; theta_source = sqrt(ab) from deconvolved FWHM axes

recipe.goal: Derive column densities by scaling to the G9.62+0.19 standard
recipe.method: N = (N_cali / I_cali) I, with I_cali the integrated (+/-5 km/s) stacked intensity of the standard spectrum and N_cali the XCLASS column density of G9.62+0.19; applied to moment maps and beam-deconvolved peak values
key_parameters: N_cali values are the Table 1 column densities of the G9.62+0.19 core used for each species
assumptions: Same excitation conditions and optically thin emission as G9.62+0.19 for all candidates

recipe.goal: Source-stack spectra of all 100 hot cores into a template spectrum
recipe.method: Extract full-band SPW 7 and 8 spectra at the stacked CH3OH peak of each core, correct the frequency axis for V_LSR, resample to 0.49 MHz channels, average with equal weights, and fit with XCLASS

recipe.goal: Correlate column densities between COM species
recipe.method: Plot column densities of molecular pairs for strong and weak cores and compute correlation coefficients

recipe.goal: Compare CH3CHO distribution with SiO and H13CO+
recipe.method: Compare moment 0 maps of stacked CH3CHO with SiO (2-1) and H13CO+ (1-0) and compute correlations of the integrated intensity maps for 43 sources where CH3CHO is as extended

answer_key.quantity: Total hot core candidates (strong + new weak)

evidence.quote: In total, we identified 100 HMC candidates, 60 of which are identical to the strong sample previously identified by (cite: 2022MNRAS.511.3463Q), and the remaining 40 are weak candidates newly identified in this work.

answer_key.quantity: Number of the 100 cores detected in each COM (CH3OH, CH3OCHO, C2H5CN, C2H5OH, CH3OCH3, CH3CHO, CH3COCH3)

evidence.quote: In total, 100 hot cores show CH$_3$OH emission, 90 show CH$_3$OCHO emission, 80 show C$_2$H$_5$CN emission, 46 show C$_2$H$_5$OH emission, 77 show CH$_3$OCH$_3$ emission, 59 show CH$_3$CHO emission, and 27 show CH$_3$COCH$_3$ emission.

answer_key.quantity: Number of the 40 new candidates with compact emission of CH3OCHO, C2H5CN, C2H5OH, CH3OCH3, CH3CHO, CH3COCH3

evidence.quote: Specifically, 36 show CH$_3$OCHO emission, 29 display C$_2$H$_5$CN emission, 5 reveal C$_2$H$_5$OH emission, 25 demonstrate CH$_3$OCH$_3$ emission, 16 present CH$_3$CHO emission, and only one core shows CH$_3$COCH$_3$ emission.
The sizes of molecular CH$_3$OH emission range from 1092 to 46884 AU for sources at different distances.
